proposal.name: Inspect fragments and stage recording files

plan.name: Inspect fragments and stage recording files
plan.summary: Add plain Go inspection that reads a whole piece, checks its opening, complete box structure and declared media bounds, and reports its duration from track timescales and sample durations, including defaults: round the longest track's duration up to positive integer milliseconds and use 4,000 ms only when no usable duration is available, independently of readability. Add separate spool operations to write and flush a caller-numbered piece, publish it by a nonreplacing hard link, discard its hidden remnant, prepare a join from caller-ordered inventory, publish the join and discard its partial output; flush directory changes, retain hidden publication evidence until explicit discard, and recognize a repeated publication by the same inode while refusing conflicting files. Join preparation reads each requested piece once through its end, omits unreadable pieces without copying any of their bytes, continues with later pieces, returns exact omitted numbers and each requested duration, and flushes only a hidden output containing the opening once and readable fragments in order with their timestamps unchanged; output errors or no readable pieces fail without publication, and originals stay untouched. Extend the existing MP4 and spool tests without changing their pinned behavior, add Linux acceptance coverage with real folders, injected I/O failures, valid synthetic boxes and all seven original writer fixture files, and keep the existing MP4 API, spool API, self-test and app recording path unchanged. Update SPEC.md and README.md to describe this tested support awaiting its callers, retain docs/PRD.md's intended behavior, leave dependencies, proved cores, models, explorers, trusted configuration and macOS entry points unchanged, and run the captured format, vet, build and test checks, with unavailable environment checks or restoration of missing original fixtures from #30 explicitly handed to a person as Merger work without skipping or claiming the compatibility test passed.

tests.name: Piece duration uses track timing and defaults
tests.says: Inspection calculates positive milliseconds from all runs and fragments, respects trun over tfhd over trex defaults, handles 32-bit and 64-bit timing and media sizes and signed offsets, preserves short pieces, and uses 4,000 ms without treating absent timing alone as unreadable.

tests.name: Inspection validates every fragment and sample extent
tests.says: A foreign prefix, incomplete or malformed box, bad run offset or short declared sample data makes a piece unreadable, including defects after an otherwise valid fragment; usable duration survives media damage.

tests.name: Inspection reads to the end and reports read failures
tests.says: Inspection consumes media and trailing boxes through the final read, handles short reads, and reports read failures even after usable timing or all declared media bytes have arrived.

tests.name: Pieces are written, published and discarded separately
tests.says: A caller can stage a positive number beyond a gap without publishing or deciding finality, publish it by hard link, repeat publication after reopening, then discard only the hidden name without replacing the closed piece.

tests.name: Interrupted writes and conflicting names preserve bytes
tests.says: An interrupted piece write never names a piece, occupied hidden and final names are not overwritten or followed through symlinks, and a different inode is a publication conflict even if its bytes match.

tests.name: Join preparation omits unreadable pieces and preserves gaps
tests.says: Preparation uses the caller's inventory beyond gaps, returns exact omissions and positive durations, includes later readable media without any bytes of omitted pieces, preserves original timestamps and pieces, and leaves the exact result hidden for separate publication.

tests.name: Join reads each requested piece once in order
tests.says: The disk input for each requested piece is opened once in order, read completely and closed once; open and late read errors omit that piece without preventing a later readable piece or leaking failed input into the output.

tests.name: Join failure and publication retries never replace files
tests.says: All-unreadable or invalid inventory fails without a named output, partial output requires explicit discard before reuse, a competing file or symlink is preserved, and the completed hard link is recognized by a fresh stager before idempotent hidden-name cleanup.

tests.name: Output failures do not publish or alter originals
tests.says: Piece staging and join preparation propagate output creation, partial write, flush and close failures, leave no named output, and permit explicit partial-output cleanup without changing closed pieces.

tests.name: Files and directory changes are flushed
tests.says: Completed hidden files are flushed before close, publication and removal flush their directory, flush failures are reported, and retries flush again even when the link or removal already happened.

tests.name: The original writer output is compatible
tests.says: All six original #30 writer pieces are readable with metadata durations 2,006, 2,006, 2,006, 2,000, 2,006 and 64 ms, and an intact staged join omits none and preserves their bytes exactly; missing or substituted original fixtures fail this test.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and 11 acceptance tests covering the complete plumbing step, including original writer compatibility and required documentation updates. The plan check passed: every acceptance test fails on the unchanged base as required, and `repo/` was left untouched.
